summary: Read all 536 lines of the markdown conversion, including references and the document ending, and checked the cited PDF pages directly with PyMuPDF. All recorded numerical statistics and total counts match the paper and the correct outcomes and arms. Table 2 confirms novelty means 3.11 versus 2.78, SDs 0.95 versus 0.96, p = .006 and d = 0.35; usefulness means 3.15 versus 2.87, SDs 0.89 versus 0.82, p = .010 and d = 0.33. Table 1 confirms condition correlations .17 (p < .01) and .16 (p < .05), with control coded 0 and LLM assistance coded 1. PDF p. 6 confirms the no-controls usefulness coefficient 0.28, SE 0.11 and p = .009. N = 250 is supported for the employee-level analyses; arm counts are not printed and correctly remain null. Construct, participant unit, more_creative direction, immediate endpoint timing, ai_vs_bau comparison, null within_person and participant se_basis are consistent with the methods. Human external scoring is confirmed, but lay/crowd versus expert qualifications are not established, so no replacement measure subtype is inferred. The five remaining problems are the same unresolved question-classification gap; null outcome_with_ai is appropriately retained rather than guessed. Coverage review under rules 4-6 found no additional identifiable eligible outcome or full-sample contrast omitted from the supplied main article. General supervisor-rated performance is not scored on an identified output; Table 3 output models include post-treatment controls; mediation and moderation analyses are excluded. The unadjusted novelty multilevel analysis has no outcome-specific coefficient, SE or exact p value in the supplied article and is already identified in not_extracted. No appendix or supplement is appended to the PDF, there are no embedded attachments, and the local supplement manifest lists no files. Requests using the specified User-Agent to https://doi.org/10.1037/apl0001296.supp and https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1037%2Fapl0001296.supp both failed with WinError 10013; separate supplement coverage remains unverified. These are alternative analyses of the same two outcomes in one sample, not five independent samples.
